advisories.title: The two new obligations characterize permission-r6-r10-input-corpus.v2, which the artifact neither pins by digest nor places under its own remeasurementClause
advisories.detail: Both new obligation reasons close with 'The NAMES-only permission-r6-r10-input-corpus.v2 does not invent those bytes and does not close this obligation.' That is three factual claims about a named third artifact, and it is the only artifact v4 relies on that carries no path and no sha256: it is absent from basedOn, absent from recordedInputs, and absent from the remeasurementClause's protected-file list, against thirteen pinned and verified references elsewhere. I resolved the artifact and checked all three claims rather than reporting an unverifiable citation as a defect in itself. It exists at docs/coop/artifacts/permission-r6-r10-input-corpus.v2.json, is 0444 and 6863 bytes, and measures 7b93dc3e — which equals the digest recorded at both ends of its own independent review, so it has not moved since being accepted. 'NAMES-only' is accurate: its whatIsAuthored states two named race initial states with no journal bytes, no expiry-age and no cleanup-bound, and its initialStates carry journalBytes, cleanupBound and expiryAge all as NOT-AUTHORED. It authors no bytes, so it cannot close an authoring obligation. Its own verdict is ACCEPT. Every claim v4 makes about it is true.
advisories.whyItStaysAdvisory: Two reasons, stated so the severity is not read as either inflated or dismissive. First, the sentence is not the ground of either classification: each obligation stands on G09 v3 naming it in leftoverDesignRemainingOnDR105, on the verbatim noteOnOblFxAuthoring, and on D-056 Decision clause 5 — all pinned and all verified. Delete the sentence and both obligations remain fully warranted. It forecloses an objection rather than carrying the claim. Second, the claim runs in the conservative direction: it keeps an obligation open, so being wrong about it could not close something that should be open. I have raised unpinned load-bearing assertions at higher severity elsewhere in this corpus, and the distinction I am drawing is deliberate — there the unpinned claim was the artifact's whole warrant and the obvious verification route returned a contradiction; here the warrant is independent and following the name leads straight to an artifact that confirms the claim.
advisories.residue: It is still a hole in v4's own custody machinery, judged by v4's own standard. The remeasurementClause enumerates which files must be unmoved for the measurement to stand and this artifact is not among them, so if the corpus is superseded the sentence silently becomes a statement about content that no longer exists there and nothing in v4 catches it. That matters more than usual in this family: the corpus's own v1 to v2 delta was a verbatim-truncation repair — r10Verbatim at 295 characters against a live 445 — so a version label alone has already proven insufficient to identify the content in this exact lineage. The author was demonstrably curating the protected list in this very edit, since G09 v3 was added to it, which makes this a fresh dependency introduced without its pin rather than an inherited omission.
advisories.whatWouldCloseIt: A path and sha256 for permission-r6-r10-input-corpus.v2 in recordedInputs, and its name in the remeasurementClause list alongside G09 v3.

So the most consequential repair in this successor is the one least documented by the mechanism the artifact uses for exactly that purpose, while three older and smaller findings retain their full disposition records. A findingDisposition entry for CLAUDE-PLJ-V3-B1 with disposition ACCEPTED and landedAt covering obligations.OBL-R10-AUTHORING, obligations.OBL-R6-AUTHORING, summary.leftoverDesign, doesNotCloseLeftoverAlone and proposedLaterWork would close it. The two v3 advisories are in the same position — A1 is substantively landed and A2 was addressed to the coordinator rather than to this artifact — and neither is dispositioned either.

independence.priorParticipation: Direct and decisive, and it is the main risk to this verdict. CLAUDE-PLJ-V3-B1 is my finding, and this successor exists to land it — so I am reviewing a repair of my own objection, where the temptation is to confirm rather than refute. Three guards. First, I verified the repair against the source rather than against my own text: the test was set equality between the subject's summary.leftoverDesign and G09 v3's leftoverDesignRemainingOnDR105 read fresh from that artifact's bytes, so the standard applied is the source's and a repair that merely matched my prose would have failed it. Second, I ran a dedicated over-correction pass, because a successor landing a blocker can fail by doing too much — I checked for invented bytes, numbers, envelopes and a fifteenth FX class, and confirmed the fourteen were byte-identical to v3's rather than trusting the artifact's statement that it did not widen them. Third, I compared all sixteen unchanged obligations field by field to confirm nothing else moved under cover of the repair. I also authored the v3 advisory on recordedInputs, which this successor lands; the same caution applies and the same method was used. What remains is that a reviewer who had not written the finding might scrutinize its repair harder than I can fully self-certify, and the coordinator should weigh that.
